sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
Growth was fastest in FY2021 and FY2022, at 17.5% and 15.8%, before slowing to 6.8% in FY2023 [D189][D238][D287].
The FY2021 step-up came from a 16% comparable sales increase, with non-foods and e-commerce particularly strong [P56][P54].
FY2022's 16% net sales growth was driven by a 14% comparable sales increase, with gasoline, business centers and travel the fastest [P42].
Operating income compounded faster than revenue at 12.3% against 10.0%, lifting operating margin from 3.2% to 3.9% [F204][F203][F23][F32].
The United States segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and 7.2pp of the 10.1% growth [D670][D672][D434].
Warehouse ancillary and other businesses contributed 3.7pp in FY2026, well above its 0.5pp in FY2025 [D601][D598].
FY2026 net sales rose 10% on an 8% comparable sales increase, with 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency [P14].
Membership fees grew 11.0% in FY2026 but contributed only 0.2pp of revenue growth [D664][D665].
Incremental operating margin was 4.7% in FY2026, so profit grew faster than revenue [D457][D435][D434].
FY2026 operating margin of 3.9% is the window high, against a 3.4% median and 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue flat [D447][D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though currency moves added $126 million of expense [P9].
Gross margin fell three basis points, with gasoline and pharmacy mix adding 19 basis points and core merchandise subtracting 11 [P12].
The effective tax rate of 24.7% left net margin at 3.0%, 0.9pp below operating margin [D420][F52][F32].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422].
That conversion sits above the 0.99x window median and the 0.83x peer median [D701][D718].
The FY2026 increase came from higher operating income and a smaller inventory investment on faster turns and better supplier terms [P6].
Capex of $6.4 billion was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F92][F10][D417][D423].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, the 100th percentile against six retail peers whose median is -4.4% [D427][D428][D715][D716].
Long-term debt fell 31.5% to $3.9 billion while cash and investments rose 39.4% [D445][F192][D453].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion absorbed 35.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was flat [D429][D430][D452].
Financing outflow of $3.4 billion covered dividends, repurchases and debt repayment [P4][F122].
Operating margin ranks in the 17th percentile against retail peers, below their 5.0% median, reflecting the membership model's thin merchandise margins [D709][D710].
Capex has grown 11.1% a year against 10.0% revenue growth, and the capex-to-D&A ratio has climbed to 2.41x [F209][F203][D423].
Receivables grew 23.6% in FY2026, far above 10.1% revenue growth, though days sales outstanding only reached 5 days [D455][D434][D431].
Current portion of debt jumped to $2.2 billion from $75 million, a refinancing item rather than a solvency one given the net cash position [X160][X159][D427].
Operating margin: a print below the 3.4% window median would reverse the FY2024-FY2026 climb, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D692][F32].
Free cash flow conversion: a fall below the 0.99x window median would signal working capital or capex pressure [D701][D422].
Warehouse ancillary growth: a return toward the 2.4% FY2025 rate would remove the 3.7pp contribution that lifted FY2026 [D597][D601].
